preview_en:
Following UEFA Nations League (UNL) relegation, Iceland begin their League C campaign against an Estonia side who’ve been able to gather some momentum in the summer months.

Match News and Current Form

Iceland haven’t enjoyed a great deal of success in the UNL to date, tumbling from League A and into the third tier for the first time ever after losing in the promotion/relegation play-offs in the last cycle. A pair of defeats against Kosovo in those play-offs were the worst possible way for new manager Arnar Gunnlaugsson’s reign to start, and things haven’t been much better since, with his side winless in six games after failing to qualify for this summer’s FIFA World Cup (D2, L4). Returning to Reykjavík isn’t guaranteed to stimulate a response either, as Iceland have only won one of the last five internationals they hosted (D2, L2).

Estonia’s 2024/25 UNL campaign was their first back in League C following promotion, and ended with a third-place finish despite losing four of their six games (W1, D1). Jürgen Henn’s side have at least won four of their last five matches (L1), lifting the Baltic Cup in June courtesy of 1-0 victories over the Faroe Islands and Lithuania, and they’ll need all the positive omens they can get here given their historical struggles at this level. Estonia have only won two of their 20 UNL games in League C (D6, L12 inc play-offs), while they’re also winless in their last seven away games at this level (D2, L5).

Head-to-Head History

This marks the pair’s first-ever competitive H2H, with Estonia having won just one of their seven previous friendly meetings (D3, L3). The last three of those have all ended level.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Only two of Iceland’s last seven games saw both teams score.

Iceland have conceded 2+ goals in seven of their last ten matches.

Three of Estonia’s last four victories inside 90 minutes were by a one-goal margin.

Estonia took a League C-low 11 corners during the last UNL campaign.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Lazio forward Albert Guðmundsson has registered six goal involvements in his last five competitive Iceland appearances (G4, A2), with five of his last seven international goals arriving after half-time. The referee may have to keep a close eye on Estonia’s Mattias Käit , who has received seven of his eight career international yellow cards in the second half.

Iceland haven’t been able to call up defender Valgeir Lunddal due to injury. Estonia’s high number of injury absentees include Vlasiy Sinyavskiy and Marten Paalberg , while Portsmouth’s Rocco Shein requested not to be called up to focus on club matters.

Betting Analysis

The hosts are overwhelming favourites to top Group C4 and achieve promotion, so Iceland to win both halves appears a sensible pick as they look to kickstart their campaign.

Author: Ben Olawumi
